context.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
context.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H E+1, with the Euclidean metric on Eucl(n+1).

record.definition: For each nonnegative integer k, Eucl(k)=R^k is the space of real k-tuples, with distance (sum_{j=1}^k |x_j-y_j|^2)^(1/2) and its Borel sigma algebra. The empty tuple is the sole point of Eucl(0). Eucl(k)×R is identified with Eucl(k+1) by adjoining the last coordinate; this identification uses the Euclidean distance sqrt(||x-y||_2^2+|t-u|^2).

record.type: diameter function on subsets of metric or extended metric spaces
record.definition: diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y): x,y in A}, as an extended nonnegative number, with supremum of the empty set zero. Thus diam(empty)=0. In ordinary Euclidean spaces a nonempty set of diameter zero is a singleton. Native ediam is this extended-valued diameter. Euclidean finite diameters are identified with their nonnegative real values.

binders.type: subset of a metric or extended metric space

record.type: positive exponent and scale Hausdorff contents and limiting Hausdorff measure on Euclidean sets
record.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of the same Euclidean space

record.type: real exponent → Borel Hausdorff measure on any extended metric space
record.definition: muH(a) denotes the native unnormalized Borel Hausdorff measure MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a. It is obtained by the metric outer-measure construction mkMetric with gauge r↦r^a on extended nonnegative diameters: at each positive scale take the maximal outer measure bounded by the gauge on all nonempty sets of at most that diameter, then take the supremum over scales and its Borel-measure realization. Values on arbitrary sets mean outer-measure values. Empty covering members cost zero and nonempty members cost diam^a with extended nonnegative-real powers; at a=0 a nonempty singleton has cost 1.

record.type: Hausdorff dimension of subsets of metric spaces, valued in [0,infinity]
record.definition: dimH(A), also written dim_H A, is the standard Hausdorff dimension: sup({a≥0 : muH(a)(A)=infinity}) in [0,infinity], where the supremum of an empty set is 0. This is the native dimH definition. The notation uses the empty-set dimension convention 0. Critical-exponent properties and agreement with the supplied positive-exponent diameter-cost measure are proof obligations, not extra assumptions.

record.type: Lebesgue measure on R and associated integral notation
record.definition: lambda is the standard Lebesgue measure on R with its Borel measurable structure and the normalization by interval length. For a Borel set J, |J| denotes lambda(J). The symbol 1_J denotes its indicator, equal to 1 on J and 0 elsewhere. Integrals of nonnegative functions are extended Lebesgue integrals (native lintegral). Restriction to I is lambda restricted to [0,1]. The usual interval values are lambda(I)=1 and lambda((a,b))=b-a for a<b; only these interval values are used.

No finiteness or sigma-finiteness assumption is required.

record.statement: For every extended metric space X with a measurable structure equal to its Borel structure, every real a and every subset A of X, muH(a)(A) = sup_{r in (0,infinity]} inf_{W:N→subsets of X, A subset union_i W(i), diam(W(i))≤r for all i} sum_i c_a(W(i)), where c_a(W(i))=diam(W(i))^a if W(i) is nonempty and c_a(empty)=0. Suprema, infima, powers and nonnegative series are extended nonnegative-real operations.

record.statement: For every nonnegative integer k, every A⊆Eucl(k), and every real a>0, H^a(A)=muH(a)(A). Consequently: a>dimH(A) implies H^a(A)=0; 0<a<dimH(A) implies H^a(A)=infinity; H^a(A)=0 implies dimH(A)≤a; and H^a(A)=infinity implies dimH(A)≥a. Hausdorff dimension is nonnegative. For A⊆B⊆Eucl(k), dimH(A)≤dimH(B). For every nonnegative integer l and every distance-preserving map g:A→Eucl(l), dimH(g(A))=dimH(A).
